tools.name: lookup_company
tools.description:
Look up one company in its official register by ID: status, address, legal form, activity, source and check date.
Use it when you have an official ID. Don't use it with a name: call search_companies first.
Inputs: country FR or ES or GB; identifier. FR: SIREN 441639465, SIRET 44163946500091, VAT FR6

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description:
Find companies by name in the official registers of France, Spain and United Kingdom, 10 per page.
Use it when you know a name but no ID, then call lookup_company or verify_company with an ID from the results. Don't use it when you already have an official ID.
Inputs: country FR or ES or GB; query,

tools.name: get_company_history
tools.description:
See what changed at a company, and when: versions with the fields that changed (address, status), each with its official source.
Use it for changes over time. Don't use it for the current state: call lookup_company.
Inputs: country FR or ES or GB; identifier as for lookup_company (441639465); option

tools.description:
Validate a company's registered address against the official address base: France via API Adresse (Base Adresse Nationale, IGN).

tools.name: list_coverage
tools.description:
List the countries, ID formats and official sources Fuentio covers. Free, no key.
Use it first when unsure whether a country or ID format is supported, or to explain coverage. Don't use it to check a company: call lookup_company or search_companies.
Inputs: none. Example: list_coverage().
Returns: p

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_company_history" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "verify_company" stacks urgency/override words (never, warning). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: lookup_company, what_changed, report_issue, get_evidence, watch_company, review_report, check_supplier_list · Private data: lookup_company, search_companies, resolve_company, explain_match, what_changed, screen_company, get_graph, report_issue, get_evidence, check_vat, watch_company, review_report, check_supplier_list · Public sink: explain_match, check_address, watch_company, check_supplier_list · Destructive: lookup_company, search_companies, get_receipt, list_coverage.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: lookup_company, what_changed, report_issue, get_evidence, watch_company, review_report, check_supplier_list · Private data: lookup_company, search_companies, resolve_company, explain_match, what_changed, screen_company, get_graph, report_issue, get_evidence, check_vat, watch_company, review_report, check_supplier_list · Public sink: explain_match, check_address, watch_company, check_supplier_list · Destructive: lookup_company, search_companies, get_receipt, list_coverage

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
